subtopics.title: How Costs Behave When Output Moves

questions.question: Variable costs are:
options: Constant per unit but growing in total as output grows
Constant in total at every output
The same as fixed costs at high volume

questions.question: Fixed costs of R560 000 at an output of 8 000 bags work out per bag to:
options: R70,00 — and the per-unit figure shrinks as output spreads the fixed total

questions.question: Mokoena's total variable cost of R64 per bag consists of:
options: Administration of R204 000 spread per bag
Direct materials R34, direct labour R22, and selling and distribution R8
The selling price less the profit

questions.question: A unit cost that includes fixed costs is only true:
options: In the first month of the year
When output is at its maximum
At the specific output it was calculated for — fixed cost per unit changes with volume

questions.question: Contribution per unit is calculated as:
options: Selling price per unit less variable cost per unit — R120 less R64 gives R56
Selling price less fixed cost per unit
Fixed costs divided by planned output

questions.question: Contribution is NOT profit because:
options: It must first pay toward the wall of fixed costs — only after they are covered does it drop through as profit
It is calculated before variable costs

questions.question: Total contribution at the planned 20 000 bags is:
The four-line factory income statement runs:
options: Sales, cost of sales, gross profit, net profit
Sales, less variable costs, contribution, less fixed costs, profit

questions.question: The break-even formula in words is:
options: Total fixed costs divided by contribution per unit
Total costs divided by selling price

questions.question: Mokoena's break-even point is:
options: 10 000 bags — R560 000 over R56 — with a break-even value of R1 200 000

questions.question: Interpreted against planned production of 20 000 bags, break-even at 10 000 means:
options: The business is already in loss
The survival line sits at exactly half the plan — a substantial cushion, with 10 000 bags earning pure profit

questions.question: If the division gives 10 001 comma 8 units, the break-even point is:
options: 10 002 units — always round UP, because at 10 001 a sliver of loss remains

questions.question: The margin of safety on the budget is:
options: 10 000 bags — 50 percent of planned sales can be lost before the loss line
5 000 bags — a quarter of the plan

questions.question: Cutting the price to R112 moves break-even to:
options: 11 667 bags — an R8 cut lands directly on the contribution and moves the line violently

questions.question: Fixed costs rising by R56 000 moves break-even to:
options: Exactly 11 000 bags — R616 000 over the unchanged R56

questions.question: The break-even model assumes:
options: Prices that fall as volume rises
Fixed costs that step with every unit
That half of production remains unsold
Constant price and unit variable cost, fixed costs that never step, and that everything made is sold

questions.question: The R560 pile of stones stands for:
options: The fixed costs — spent before plate one, the same whether you sell nothing or a mountain
The cost of the steak and pap
The selling price of ten plates

questions.question: The R64 that travels with every plate is:
options: The variable cost per unit — steak, pap, chakalaka, container

questions.question: Each plate sold at R120 lifts how much off the pile?
options: R56 — the contribution: one stone per plate

questions.question: Busy sellers win twice because:
options: Their ingredients get cheaper per plate
Fixed costs disappear at high volume
More contributions arrive AND the fixed cost per plate thins as volume spreads it

questions.question: With a pile of R560 and R56 lifted per plate, the pile is gone at:
options: Plate ten — and plate eleven is the first sold purely for yourself

questions.question: If the division gives ten comma four plates, you break even on:
options: Plate eleven — round the survival line UP; at ten you are still a stone short

questions.question: Expecting to sell eleven plates with break-even at ten means:
options: One rained-out match from a loss — the line only means something next to what you expect to sell

questions.question: The factory's version of plate number ten is:
options: Bag 10 000 — the same formula with more zeros

subtopics.title: When the Price of Meat Goes Up

questions.question: Steak up R4 a plate changes the survival line by:
options: Contribution drops to R52, so the line moves from ten to eleven plates
Nothing — meat is a fixed cost
The price must rise by R4

questions.question: An R8 discount on a R120 plate feels small but:
options: It takes one seventh of the contribution — price cuts bite the contribution, not the price

questions.question: A fixed-cost rise and a variable-cost rise move the line by different routes:
options: One grows the pile to be cleared; the other shrinks every unit's stone-lifting power

questions.question: Break-even analysis is called a headlight because:
options: It only works in the dark season
It prices decisions BEFORE they are made — canvas, contracts and rent are tested before anyone signs
